summary.intent: Understand the memory loop architecture, then design and begin implementing an MCP server that allows Claude to pull memories on demand as an alternative to hook-based injection.
summary.outcome: Architecture questions fully answered; MCP server design spec written and approved; implementation plan created; Tasks 1-4 of 8 completed (dependency added, server scaffold with mode gating, search_memories handler, save_memory handler in progress).

repo: Memory loop has two independent axes: mode (off/manual/auto controls injection) and activation_policy (review/auto controls whether generated memories become active or stay candidate).
Refresh is always manual — 'auto' mode only controls hook-based injection at turn start, not generation.
Repo-scope memories always require explicit promotion regardless of activation_policy, as a governance guard against one person's memories steering everyone's Claude sessions.
The project had no existing MCP server — Claude Code interacted with the CLI purely through hooks (push model); MCP adds a pull model.
manual mode currently has no compelling use case; with MCP it gains identity: no hook push but Claude can pull via MCP on demand.
AddManualRecord sets Status: StatusActive for manual records, not StatusCandidate — save_memory handler needed to bypass this and create candidates directly.
fingerprintForRecord needed to be exported for the save_memory dedup pre-check.

code.finding: Injection gate: if mode != ModeAuto, maybeInjectMemoryLoop returns nil immediately — no manual injection mechanism exists.
AddManualRecord sets Status: StatusActive (not StatusCandidate) and handles dedup via findReconcileIndex — incompatible with spec requirement for save_memory to create candidates.
PreviewSelection is too restrictive for MCP search — filters out candidates via passesInjectionGate and returns empty on empty queries. Search handler needs its own filter+score path.

workflow: t.Parallel() cannot be combined with t.Chdir() in Go tests — causes panic; subagent caught this deviation correctly.
When a new package imports an external library, go.mod/go.sum only update when the import is first added to source code, not when go get is run alone.
Subagent-driven development pattern used: dispatch implementer per task with full context, verify tests pass, then mark complete before proceeding to next task.

friction: SelectRelevant/PreviewSelection reuse was blocked by passesInjectionGate — search handler needed a custom filter+score path that couldn't reuse existing injection code directly.
AddManualRecord's hardcoded StatusActive conflicted with the spec's StatusCandidate requirement for save_memory, requiring either bypassing it or exporting fingerprintForRecord.
User interrupted the plan writing twice mid-stream, requiring 'continue' prompts to resume.
mcp-go library API had to be fetched via context7 MCP tool since it wasn't in the codebase — added lookup overhead.
open_items: Task 4 (save_memory handler) was in progress at transcript end — export of fingerprintForRecord and handler implementation not yet verified.
